summary: Sh. Ali Mashhour continues discussing the Quranic story of Prophet Ibrahim and his son Ismail from Sahih Bukhari and Sahih Muslim. He explains how Ismail grew up in Mecca, learned Arabic and archery, and married a local woman. When Ibrahim returned to check on his son as a young man, he found Ismail's wife complaining about their difficult living conditions. Ibrahim commanded Ismail to divorce her, citing the poor state of their home's threshold as evidence of her inadequate care. Sh. Ali Mashhour uses this narrative to teach about filial piety and explores the scholarly consensus on when children must obey their parents' commands to divorce, concluding that obedience is obligatory only when parental guidance is rooted in Islamic knowledge and piety rather than personal preference.
